name: Excimer laser for stretch marks

angle.text: The 308 nm excimer laser, used in dermatology for vitiligo and psoriasis, has been tried on white stretch marks to restore pigment so they blend in. The evidence is a tiny early-phase study.

summary: A UV laser aimed at repigmenting white stretch marks; the sources show only a tiny early-phase study.
note: Only a 10-person phase 1 registration was found; no published results were reviewed.
currentQuick:
The excimer laser is a 308 nm ultraviolet device used in dermatology, and it has been tried on stretch marks that have faded to white.
The sources reviewed show one small phase 1 trial registration without listed results, so the effect on stretch marks is not established here.
How it works: Proponents say the ultraviolet light stimulates pigment-producing cells in the pale marks so they darken toward the surrounding skin tone.
Risks and caveats: The sources reviewed give no safety data for this use. Ultraviolet treatments in general carry considerations that clinicians weigh, but none are documented in the sources used for this article.
deepLead:
The 308 nm excimer laser is an ultraviolet light device that is used in dermatology for conditions such as vitiligo and psoriasis. It has also been studied for white (mature) stretch marks, striae alba, which are pale because the skin has lost pigment .
Stretch marks begin red or purple and later fade to a pale, atrophic appearance . Proponents of excimer treatment say the ultraviolet light stimulates pigment cells to repigment white marks. Wikipedia, citing a 2014 systematic review, states that no stretch-mark treatment has been clearly shown to be effective once marks have formed, and it does not discuss excimer laser specifically .
The sources reviewed include one small registered study, a 10-person phase 1 trial of 308 nm excimer laser in white striae, with no results listed in the registry record .

name: PRP for stretch marks

angle.text: Concentrated platelets from a person's own blood are applied or injected, often with microneedling or lasers, to improve stretch marks. Proponents cite collagen remodelling, and the evidence is small trials mostly of PRP as an add-on.

summary: Concentrated platelets from your own blood, tried on stretch marks mostly as an add-on in small trials.
note: Registered studies are small and mostly combine PRP with other treatments; no results were reviewed.
currentQuick:
PRP is made from a person's own blood and has been tried on stretch marks, usually together with microneedling, lasers or fat grafting.
The sources reviewed are a handful of small registered trials with no listed results, so its effect on stretch marks is not established here.
How it works: Proponents say platelet growth factors stimulate collagen and tissue repair in the skin.
Risks and caveats: The sources reviewed give no safety data. As a blood-derived injectable procedure, it is performed by clinicians.
deepLead:
Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) for stretch marks involves processing a person's own blood to concentrate platelets and applying or injecting the product into stretch marks (striae distensae), often with microneedling or lasers. Proponents say the growth factors in platelets encourage collagen remodelling.
Wikipedia notes that stretch marks form from stretching of the dermis and that, according to a 2014 systematic review, no treatment has been clearly effective once they have formed; PRP is not discussed there .
Clinical research is limited to small registered trials, several of which combine PRP with another modality such as fractional lasers or fat grafting, making the effect of PRP alone hard to isolate. The registry records reviewed list no results .

name: Subcision / TCA CROSS

chain: Depressed scar lifts and collagen forms
angle.text: Subcision is used for rolling, tethered acne scars to release them and lift the skin, and TCA CROSS is a related acid-based scar procedure. Small studies and reviews support subcision as part of combined care.

summary: A needle procedure that cuts the fibres tying rolling acne scars down; small studies and reviews support it as part of combined care.
note: Performed by clinicians; forum accounts of self-performed procedures exist but are not described here.
currentQuick:
Subcision uses a needle under the skin to release the bands that tether depressed acne scars, described in 1995. TCA CROSS is a separate acid-based scar procedure often mentioned alongside it.
Dermatology reviews treat subcision as one part of multimodality scar care, with studies mostly small case series and registered trials.
How it works: Cutting the fibrous tether is described as letting the scar rise, with a wound-healing response adding collagen.
Risks and caveats: Grokipedia lists bleeding disorders, infection and keloid tendency as contraindications. Sources reviewed give limited complication data.
deepLead:
Subcision is a minor surgical procedure for depressed (atrophic) scars in which a needle is inserted beneath the skin and moved to cut the fibrous bands that hold a scar down. It was named and described in 1995 by Orentreich and Orentreich as subcutaneous incisionless surgery for depressed scars and wrinkles . TCA CROSS (chemical reconstruction of skin scars) is a separate scar procedure that uses trichloroacetic acid; it is grouped with subcision in community discussion of scar treatment, but the sources reviewed for this article do not describe it in detail.
Subcision is mainly applied to rolling acne scars, which dermatologists classify as one of three atrophic scar types alongside icepick and boxcar scars . It has also been studied for cellulite . Reviews of acne-scar management describe it as one component of multimodality treatment tailored to scar type .
On looksmax.org, subcision is discussed as a step used when other treatments have not improved tethered scars, and the forum includes self-performed ('DIY') accounts. This article documents that the practice is discussed but does not describe how to perform it.

name: Cortisone injections for keloids

angle.text: Clinic-administered corticosteroid injection, often triamcinolone, is a long-standing option to flatten raised keloid scars. It is now being compared with newer agents in small trials.

summary: A clinic-administered steroid injection into keloids, a long-standing option now being compared with newer agents in small trials.
note: Prescription clinical procedure; case reports describe reactions, and no outcomes from the listed trials were reviewed.
currentQuick:
A corticosteroid, usually triamcinolone, is injected into a keloid by a clinician to reduce inflammation, itching and fibroblast activity. Wikipedia lists it among standard keloid options.
Current registered trials compare it with fluorouracil, metformin, lasers and botulinum toxin.
How it works: Corticosteroids are described as reducing fibroblast activity and inflammation in the scar.
Risks and caveats: A case report describes a reaction after injection with lidocaine. Systematic adverse-event data were not in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Intralesional corticosteroid injection, commonly with triamcinolone acetonide, is a treatment in which a corticosteroid is injected directly into a keloid, a raised scar that grows beyond the original wound. Wikipedia reports that intralesional corticosteroids were introduced in the mid-1960s and are said to reduce fibroblast activity, inflammation and itching .
Keloids are most common in people of sub-Saharan African, Asian or Latin American ancestry, often appear between ages 10 and 20, and frequently follow piercing, particularly of the earlobes . Wikipedia describes corticosteroid injection as one of several options, sometimes combined with 5-fluorouracil and pulsed dye laser in adults .
Registered clinical trials continue to compare steroid injection with other agents, including 5-fluorouracil, metformin, botulinum toxin and laser-assisted delivery. A published case report documents a reaction after an injection of triamcinolone with lidocaine .

name: Keloid surgery + radiation

angle.text: Surgical removal of a keloid, followed by radiation to lower recurrence, is a clinical standard for severe cases, and the removal itself is visible. Excision alone has high recurrence, and add-on studies show lower rates.

summary: Cutting out a keloid and radiating the wound bed, a clinical standard for severe cases with many add-on studies.
note: Surgical alone recurrence is reported at 70 to 100 percent; radiation is not recommended for children per Wikipedia.
currentQuick:
The keloid is surgically removed and the area is treated with radiation to lower regrowth. Wikipedia reports very high recurrence after excision alone and lower recurrence with radiation or other adjuncts.
Studies examine add-ons such as steroid injection, hyperbaric oxygen and botulinum toxin.
How it works: Surgery removes the scar tissue; radiation is used to suppress renewed fibroblast growth in the wound.
Risks and caveats: Recurrence, sometimes larger, is the main documented problem; radiation is not recommended in children for growth reasons per Wikipedia.
deepLead:
Keloid excision with adjuvant radiation therapy is a combination in which a keloid is surgically removed and the wound is then treated with radiation to reduce regrowth. Wikipedia reports that excision alone has a recurrence rate of 70 to 100 percent, that recurrences can be larger, and that adding radiation, pressure therapy or laser sharply lowers recurrence; it adds that radiation is not recommended for children because of growth-abnormality risk .
Published studies describe surgery plus radiotherapy as a standard approach for severe keloids; one 2020 paper states that radiotherapy is essential for preventing recurrence . Researchers also study adjuncts: hyperbaric oxygen, steroid injection, botulinum toxin, photobiomodulation and tension-reducing suturing .
Keloids most often affect people of sub-Saharan African, Asian or Latin American ancestry and commonly follow earlobe piercing .

name: Mederma / onion extract scar gel

angle.text: Users apply this over-the-counter onion extract gel to surgical, burn and acne scars, and some forum posters claim it helps old pockmarks. Trial evidence is mixed and limited.

summary: Over-the-counter onion extract scar gel with mixed, limited trial evidence.
note: Trial results are mixed; scar types and study sizes vary.
currentQuick:
Mederma is a widely sold over-the-counter gel containing onion bulb extract, marketed for improving the look of surgical, injury and acne scars.
Trial evidence is limited and mixed: some studies compare it with plain emollients, and secondary sources describe both positive and null findings.
How it works: The maker describes moisturizing, cell renewal and collagen support. Laboratory literature associates onion flavonoids with anti-inflammatory activity; human mechanisms are not established in the sources reviewed.
Risks and caveats: It is for external use on healed skin, away from eyes and open wounds, per product labelling. No serious adverse events are described in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Mederma is an over-the-counter brand of topical scar products whose best-known product, Mederma Advanced Scar Gel, contains an extract of onion bulb (Allium cepa) together with other ingredients such as allantoin. It is marketed for improving the appearance of scars from surgery, injury, burns and acne.
The brand was introduced in the United States in 1997 by Merz Pharmaceuticals and later passed to HRA Pharma (2019) and then Perrigo, according to one AI-generated encyclopedia summary. Manufacturer claims of visible improvement in scar texture, colour and softness after weeks to months of daily use are described there.
Published evidence is limited and mixed. A randomized, double-blind comparison of onion extract gel with a petrolatum-based emollient on new surgical scars has been published, a rabbit-ear scar model study examined the product, and several small trials are registered on ClinicalTrials.gov. Clinical references such as Wikipedia describe silicone, pressure, massage and steroid injection as the more commonly discussed scar treatments, and mention onion extract mainly as a comparator.

name: Bio-Oil

chain: Scars and stretch marks look softer
angle.text: Users apply this popular cosmetic oil to scars, stretch marks and uneven skin tone. No product-specific evidence was found for these uses.

summary: Popular scar and stretch mark oil with no product-specific evidence found here.
note: Sources for this product were thin.
currentQuick:
Bio-Oil is a branded cosmetic oil marketed for scars and stretch marks.
Sources reviewed contain no product-specific trials; general references say creams and oils have not been shown to prevent stretch marks in pregnancy.
How it works: Moisturizing oils soften skin surface; no mechanism for changing scar or stretch mark structure was established in the sources reviewed.
Risks and caveats: No safety data were found in the sources reviewed. As a cosmetic, it is not subject to drug approval.
deepLead:
Bio-Oil is a commercial skincare oil marketed for improving the appearance of scars, stretch marks and uneven skin tone. It is a branded cosmetic product, not a drug.
Peer-reviewed literature on the specific product was not available to this wiki at the time of writing, so the evidence summary below is limited to what general references say about stretch marks. A Wikipedia summary reports a Cochrane systematic review finding no evidence that creams or oils prevent or reduce stretch marks in pregnancy.

name: Cocoa butter / shea / coconut oil

angle.text: These plant fats are a traditional folk choice for trying to prevent stretch marks, especially in pregnancy. Reviews found no evidence that they prevent marks.

summary: Folk stretch mark moisturizers; reviews found no evidence they prevent marks.
note: Used as moisturizers; stretch mark prevention not shown.
currentQuick:
These plant fats are common moisturizing ingredients and a traditional choice for preventing stretch marks.
A registered trial of cocoa butter exists, but reviews summarized on Wikipedia report no evidence that creams or oils prevent stretch marks.
How it works: They act as emollients that soften and hydrate the skin surface; no mechanism for preventing stretch marks is established.
Risks and caveats: Sources reviewed describe no specific harms; individual skin reactions to any topical product are possible.
deepLead:
Cocoa butter, shea butter and coconut oil are plant fats widely used in moisturizers, soaps and lotions, and are a traditional folk choice for trying to prevent stretch marks in pregnancy.
A Wikipedia summary reports that a Cochrane review found no evidence that creams or oils prevent or reduce stretch marks in pregnancy. A registered randomized trial of cocoa butter for stretch marks in pregnancy exists.

name: Folliculitis shower hygiene (post-gym shower)

chain: Less sweat and bacteria on skin
angle.text: Some people shower soon after sweating to reduce body acne and folliculitis on the back and chest. General references suggest the habit, though trials have not tested it.

summary: Showering after sweat to limit body acne; suggested in general references, untested in trials.
note: No controlled studies found.
currentQuick:
Some people shower soon after sweating to reduce body acne and folliculitis.
General references suggest it as a measure against acne mechanica, but no controlled study was found.
How it works: The practice aims to remove sweat, oil and surface bacteria that can irritate follicles.
Risks and caveats: No harms are described; over-washing or harsh cleansers can irritate skin per general advice.
deepLead:
Showering soon after sweating is a hygiene habit that some people adopt to reduce body acne ("bacne") and folliculitis.
Wikipedia describes folliculitis as inflammation of hair follicles, most often from Staphylococcus aureus, with friction from clothing, blocked follicles and shaving listed as triggers. The article on acne mechanica lists heat, friction and pressure as causes and mentions showering soon after exercise as a suggestion, while noting that the page itself is flagged for needing better medical sources.

name: Loose cotton clothing / washing sheets

angle.text: Users wear loose, breathable cotton and wash bedding regularly to reduce friction and occlusion acne on the body. The habit is suggested generally and untested.

summary: Loose cotton and clean bedding to cut friction acne; suggested generally, untested.
note: No controlled studies found.
currentQuick:
Some people wear loose cotton and wash sheets often to reduce acne from rubbing and trapped sweat.
General references suggest loose breathable fabric for acne mechanica; no trials were found.
How it works: Looser, breathable fabric reduces friction, heat and sweat retention on skin.
Risks and caveats: No harms are described.
deepLead:
Wearing loose, breathable clothing such as cotton and washing bedding regularly are habits adopted to reduce friction- and occlusion-related acne.
Wikipedia says acne mechanica arises from friction, heat and pressure, and suggests loose-fitting, breathable fabrics such as cotton over synthetics; the page is flagged as needing more reliable medical sources. It also lists clothing friction as a trigger of folliculitis.

name: Chlorhexidine / antibacterial body wash

angle.text: Users apply antibacterial washes such as chlorhexidine to calm body folliculitis, aiming for smoother, clearer skin on the back, chest and shoulders. It is studied in hospitals for bacterial decolonization; its use for folliculitis bumps rests on anecdote.

summary: Hospital antiseptic wash used by some for body folliculitis; no trials for that use.
note: Can irritate skin; avoid eyes and ears per labelling.
currentQuick:
Chlorhexidine is an antiseptic widely used in surgery and hospitals, also sold as a skin wash.
Its evidence is from surgical and ICU settings; none was found for cosmetic folliculitis.
How it works: It binds bacterial cell walls and disrupts membranes.
Risks and caveats: Skin irritation and allergic reactions are reported; eye and ear contact can cause damage.
deepLead:
Chlorhexidine is a cationic bisbiguanide antiseptic used on skin, wounds, in dentistry and on medical equipment, and it is available over the counter in the United States. Chlorhexidine washes are used in healthcare for Staphylococcus aureus decolonization, and some people use antibacterial body washes for body folliculitis.
Evidence for chlorhexidine washes comes mainly from surgical and hospital settings; no trial of its use for cosmetic body folliculitis was found.

name: Antibiotics (doxycycline) for back acne

angle.text: Doxycycline is prescribed for moderate to severe acne, and people with inflamed back and body acne use it to clear lesions and reduce marks. Acne is a studied use of the drug, with guidelines favouring short courses alongside non-antibiotic treatments.

summary: A prescription tetracycline antibiotic widely used for inflamed body acne; guidelines favour short courses alongside non-antibiotic treatments.
note: Prescription-only; photosensitivity, GI effects and antibiotic-resistance concerns are documented; not for pregnancy.
currentQuick:
Doxycycline is a tetracycline-class antibiotic that clinicians prescribe for moderate to severe inflammatory acne, including acne on the back and chest. Part of its effect is thought to come from anti-inflammatory action rather than killing bacteria alone.[1][2]
In looksmaxxing and skin-care communities it is discussed as an oral option for stubborn back acne, usually alongside topical treatments. Dermatology guidance cited on Wikipedia generally recommends limiting oral antibiotic courses to about three months and combining them with other agents.[3]
How it works: Doxycycline blocks bacterial protein synthesis by binding the 30S ribosomal subunit.[1] In acne and rosacea, anti-inflammatory and anti-angiogenic effects are also thought to contribute, and lower sub-antimicrobial doses are used for this reason.[2]
Risks and caveats: Common effects include nausea, diarrhoea and increased sunburn risk; pill esophagitis can occur if swallowed with too little fluid, and use with isotretinoin or other retinoids is contraindicated because of intracranial hypertension risk.[2] The US label warns of tooth discoloration with use during tooth development and lists pregnancy concerns.[4] Prolonged use is associated with antibiotic-resistant skin bacteria.[3] It is prescription-only in the US and UK.
deepLead:
Doxycycline is a synthetic, broad-spectrum antibiotic of the tetracycline class, developed by Pfizer and first marketed as Vibramycin in 1967. It treats a wide range of bacterial infections and is also prescribed for moderate to severe acne vulgaris.
In appearance communities it is discussed as an oral treatment for inflammatory acne on the back, chest and shoulders (often called truncal acne or "bacne"), typically for cases where topical products have not been enough. Its acne benefit is attributed partly to anti-inflammatory effects in addition to its action against bacteria.
Dermatology guidance summarised on Wikipedia describes oral antibiotics as faster-acting than topical ones for inflamed lesions, but recommends limiting courses to about three months and pairing them with benzoyl peroxide or a retinoid to limit bacterial resistance. Doxycycline is prescription-only in the United States and United Kingdom.

name: Sunless tan / body makeup to hide marks

angle.text: Self-tanner and body makeup visibly blend stretch marks and scars into surrounding skin for the day or week. The color change is immediate and measurable, and users apply it before beach days, photos or shirtless occasions.

summary: Self-tanner and body makeup that visually blend stretch marks and scars; the effect is temporary and cosmetic.
note: Color fades in days and gives no UV protection; DHA is not approved for inhalation or use around eyes and lips.
currentQuick:
Sunless tanners and body makeup are used to reduce the contrast between marks such as stretch marks or scars and the surrounding skin. Tanners darken the surface skin chemically, while bronzers and makeup add temporary color that washes off.[1][2]
The effects last from hours (makeup, bronzer) to roughly a week (DHA tanners), and no controlled studies of these products specifically for hiding stretch marks or scars were found.
How it works: DHA (dihydroxyacetone), typically 3 to 5 percent in products, reacts with amino acids in the dead outer layer of skin to produce a brown color that fades over about 3 to 10 days. Bronzers and camouflage makeup are pigments that sit on the skin and wash off.[1][2]
Risks and caveats: A tan from DHA does not protect against UV, and sunscreen added to tanners wears off quickly.[1] The FDA has approved DHA for external use but not for the eyes, lips, mucous membranes or inhalation; contact dermatitis has been reported, and laboratory studies have reported DNA damage and free-radical formation, though a 2010 EU scientific committee opinion found spray tanning posed no risk.[1]
deepLead:
Sunless tanning and body makeup are cosmetic ways to visually mask uneven skin color, including stretch marks (striae) and scars, without a procedure. Sunless tanners darken the skin with a reactive ingredient, usually dihydroxyacetone (DHA), while bronzers and camouflage makeup apply removable pigment.
Wikipedia's article on cosmetic camouflage lists acne, scars, stretch marks, vitiligo, tattoos and bruises among conditions that such creams are used to conceal, and says camouflage may reduce the psychological impact of skin imperfections, without presenting clinical efficacy data. Published trials of sunless tanner specifically for hiding stretch marks or scars were not found.

name: Dermablend / tattoo cover

angle.text: Camouflage makeup such as Dermablend is used to conceal tattoos, scars, vitiligo patches and bruises with heavier coverage than foundation. The concealing effect is visible as soon as it is applied and lasts until it is washed off.

summary: High-coverage camouflage makeup used to hide tattoos, scars and discoloration; effects are cosmetic and temporary.
note: No clinical efficacy data found; coverage wears off and needs reapplication.
currentQuick:
Dermablend is a brand of high-coverage camouflage makeup, and "tattoo cover" refers to concealers of this type used to mask tattoos, scars, birthmarks and discoloration on the face or body.
Wikipedia describes cosmetic camouflage as creams or powders that hide color or texture irregularities, first developed by plastic surgeons during World War II for burns. No published trials of specific products were found.
How it works: Opaque, pigment-rich creams or powders are applied over the skin to match surrounding skin tone and hide underlying color. Color-correcting shades such as green are suggested to neutralise redness.[1]
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia's article does not list specific risks. As with other cosmetics, ingredients can cause irritation or allergic reactions in some people, and the makeup wears off and must be reapplied.
deepLead:
Tattoo cover products are camouflage makeups designed to conceal tattoos, scars, vitiligo patches, bruises and other skin irregularities with heavier coverage than everyday foundation. Dermablend is one commercial brand in this category.
Wikipedia's cosmetic camouflage article says these creams were first developed by plastic surgeons during World War II to cover severe burns on pilots, and that the approach may reduce the psychological impact of skin imperfections; the article gives no clinical efficacy data and does not discuss specific brands.

name: Scar tattooing / micropigmentation

angle.text: Micropigmentation deposits skin-toned pigment into scars or pale patches so they blend with surrounding skin, and it is used after surgery and for vitiligo. The color match is visible once healed; published outcome data are limited to clinical documentation.

summary: Cosmetic tattooing that deposits pigment in scars or pale skin to blend them with surrounding skin; documented clinically but with little outcome data.
note: Pigment is semi-permanent and matching skin tone is difficult; the Wikipedia overview gives no outcome data.
currentQuick:
Scar tattooing, or micropigmentation, places pigment into the skin to make scars, pale patches or missing structures such as an areola look more like the surrounding skin. It belongs to the broader field of medical tattooing.[1]
Sources reviewed describe uses and history but give no controlled outcome data, and the evidence base cited by Wikipedia consists mainly of patient satisfaction reviews and general reviews of medical tattooing.
How it works: A tattoo device deposits pigment in the dermis, in a realistic style meant to imitate normal skin color. For scars, people may alternatively choose a decorative design that covers the area.[1]
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia's article does not detail risks specific to scar camouflage. It notes that diabetes can impair wound healing, so timing and location of a medical tattoo may need care in people with diabetes.[1] General tattoo risks include infection and allergic reactions.
deepLead:
Scar tattooing, also called micropigmentation, is a form of medical tattooing intended to hide a medical condition or the result of its treatment, typically in a realistic style. It is used to camouflage scars, reduce the visibility of vitiligo patches, and recreate areolas after mastectomy or chest surgery.
In looksmaxxing discussions it appears among "hardmaxxing" procedures for scars. Published information reviewed here describes its history and uses but offers little outcome data; Wikipedia cites a 2021 systematic review of patient satisfaction and older reviews of medical tattooing without summarising their findings.

name: Stretch mark surgery / tummy tuck

angle.text: Abdominoplasty removes excess abdominal skin and tightens the muscle, so stretch marks on the removed skin go with it and the midsection looks flatter. People seek it after pregnancy or major weight loss, and the change is visible after healing.

summary: Abdominoplasty removes loose abdominal skin and tightens muscle; stretch marks on removed skin go with it, but it is major surgery with a notable complication rate.
note: Major surgery under general anaesthesia; complication rates exceed many other cosmetic procedures and it leaves a hip-to-hip scar.
currentQuick:
A tummy tuck (abdominoplasty) removes excess skin and fat from the abdomen and tightens the abdominal wall. In some discussions it is raised as a way to excise skin carrying stretch marks, mainly below the navel.
It is usually sought after pregnancy or major weight loss, and is described as primarily cosmetic with some reconstructive benefits for skin folds and muscle separation.[1][2]
How it works: Skin and fat from the mid and lower abdomen are excised through a hip-to-hip incision above the pubic area, the underlying muscle fascia is tightened, and the navel is repositioned.[2] Stretch marks are only removed if they lie within the excised skin; the article sources do not address striae directly.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia reports complication rates higher than many other cosmetic surgeries, including seroma, hematoma, infection, wound separation, necrosis, thick or widened scars, numbness, blood clots and anesthesia complications; smoking, obesity and diabetes raise risk.[2] Grokipedia lists general anesthesia, 2 to 5 hours of operating time and recovery of weeks to months.[1]
deepLead:
Abdominoplasty, commonly called a tummy tuck, is a surgical procedure that removes excess skin and fat from the abdomen and tightens the underlying muscle and fascia. It is typically sought after pregnancy or major weight loss, including after bariatric surgery, when loose skin and stretched abdominal muscles persist despite diet and exercise.
In looksmaxxing and body-image discussions it is mentioned as a surgical option for stretch marks on lower abdominal skin, since the marks are removed if they lie within the excised tissue. Wikipedia and Grokipedia describe the operation chiefly as a contouring procedure and do not discuss striae removal specifically.
The surgery is described as generally safe and effective when performed by qualified plastic surgeons, but with complication rates higher than many other cosmetic surgeries because of the extent of dissection.

name: Slow bulking / slow growth to avoid stretch marks

angle.text: Lifters gain size gradually in the belief that it lowers the chance of stretch marks on shoulders, arms and chest while building a bigger physique. Rapid growth is a recognised risk factor for striae, but no trial has tested slow bulking itself.

summary: Gaining weight or muscle gradually in the belief that it lowers the chance of stretch marks; rapid growth is a recognised risk factor, but no trial has tested slow bulking.
note: Genetics and hormones also influence striae; no trials of gain rate on stretch marks were found.
currentQuick:
Some lifters and growing teenagers aim to gain size slowly to reduce the chance of stretch marks (striae). The idea rests on the understanding that striae are scars caused by the skin stretching quickly.[1]
Wikipedia lists weight gain (fat or muscle), adolescent growth spurts, pregnancy and bodybuilding among risk factors, alongside genetics and hormones. No study was found that tests whether a slower rate of gain changes the incidence.
How it works: Stretch marks appear to be caused by stretching of the skin, with tearing of the dermis; elevated cortisol, which can reduce collagen and elastin production, is also implicated.[1] Slow gain is proposed to give skin more time to adapt.
Risks and caveats: Slow bulking itself carries no particular documented harm. Wikipedia reports that a Cochrane review found no evidence that creams or oils prevent stretch marks in pregnancy, and no clearly useful treatment exists once they form.[1]
deepLead:
Slow bulking, or slow growth, refers to gaining weight or muscle gradually with the aim of avoiding stretch marks (striae). Stretch marks are dermal scars thought to be caused by rapid stretching of the skin.
Wikipedia lists rapid weight gain, adolescent growth spurts, pregnancy, bodybuilding and hormone therapy among recognised risk factors, with genetics and conditions that raise cortisol also contributing. No published trial was found comparing different rates of weight or muscle gain with stretch mark incidence.

name: Cellulite lasers / Cellfina

angle.text: Cellfina and laser devices are used to smooth cellulite dimples on the thighs and buttocks. Cellfina has 3-year follow-up data for dimple-type cellulite, while evidence for lasers is thinner.

summary: Office procedures that cut or heat the bands behind cellulite dimples; one subcision device has 3-year follow-up data, but evidence for lasers is thinner.
note: Best suited to dimple-type cellulite according to treating clinicians.
currentQuick:
Cellfina is a device-guided subcision procedure for dimple-type cellulite. Laser and other energy devices are discussed alongside it as options.
A pivotal study followed Cellfina patients for three years and reported sustained improvement; evidence for laser treatments is not covered in the available sources.
How it works: Subcision releases the fibrous bands that tether the skin and create dimples; Cellfina does this with a tissue-stabilized, guided device.
Risks and caveats: It is a minimally invasive in-office procedure; clinicians note patient selection matters because not all body contour concerns are dimple-type cellulite. Complication data are not detailed in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Cellulite lasers and Cellfina are in-office procedures aimed at the dimpled skin surface that many people, mostly women, notice on the thighs and buttocks. Cellfina is a tissue-stabilized, guided subcision device that mechanically releases the fibrous bands under the skin that are associated with dimple-type cellulite . Laser and other energy-based devices are a separate group of treatments that are discussed alongside it .
In looksmaxxing communities the topic sits at the edge of body-focused hardmaxxing, and the available published research comes from the dermatology literature rather than from forums. A pivotal open-label multicenter study followed Cellfina patients for three years and reported sustained improvement in the appearance of cellulite . Treatment authors also note that the device is best suited to dimple-type cellulite and that patients often label other body features as cellulite .

name: Body shaving / hair removal for skin texture

angle.text: Men shave the chest, arms, legs or back to look smoother and to show muscle definition, especially for physique photos and competitions. The smoother look is visible straight away and is treated in appearance communities as a style choice.

summary: Shaving or removing body hair to look smoother; a grooming choice with minor skin irritation risks and little dedicated research.
note: Reported effects include razor burn, bumps and ingrown hairs; one MRSA outbreak report cites cosmetic shaving.
currentQuick:
Body shaving is hair removal on the torso or limbs for a smoother or more defined look. It is a style practice, not a treatment.
Little research addresses it for skin texture specifically.
How it works: Razors or trimmers cut hair at the skin surface; hair removal is temporary.
Risks and caveats: Cuts, razor burn, razor bumps and ingrown hairs are reported; an MRSA outbreak in a football team was linked in part to cosmetic body shaving.
deepLead:
Body shaving and hair removal, in this context, means removing chest, arm, leg or back hair to make skin look smoother or to show muscle definition. It is discussed in appearance communities as a style practice rather than a medical treatment. Men most often shave facial hair, and some also shave the chest, abdomen, underarms, legs or pubic area .
Published research on cosmetic body shaving is limited. One well-known investigation described an outbreak of MRSA skin infections among players on a college football team in which cosmetic body shaving and turf burns were identified as facilitating factors .

name: Brazilian tan / spray tan to even skin

angle.text: Spray tans apply a DHA solution to evens out skin tone and give a bronzed look that lasts about a week. The color is visible within hours and is used before events, shoots and competitions.

summary: A DHA-based temporary skin color applied by spray to even out tone; lasts about a week and offers no UV protection.
note: FDA approves DHA for external use only, not inhalation or mucous membranes.
currentQuick:
A spray tan applies DHA to temporarily color the skin and give a more even bronze look without UV exposure.
Results fade over several days as the outer skin sheds.
How it works: DHA reacts with amino acids in the dead outer layer of skin to produce brown color.
Risks and caveats: The FDA approves DHA for external use only; contact dermatitis and inhalation concerns are reported, and the tan does not protect against UV.
deepLead:
Spray tanning is a sunless tanning method in which a dihydroxyacetone (DHA) solution is applied to the skin to produce a temporary bronze color, used in appearance communities to even out skin tone. DHA reacts with amino acids in the dead outer skin layer rather than acting as a dye .
A 2005 review described DHA as the only sunless tanning ingredient approved by the FDA and described spray-on products as delivering the formulation evenly to give a full-body tan without ultraviolet exposure .
